# Marko Lošić

> QA Engineer based in Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina, with 6+ years in manual and automated testing of web apps, mobile apps and browser extensions. Currently QA Engineer at Bravo System (Playwright with C#, Maestro, LLM testing); previously QA Engineer & Oracle APEX Developer at Krajina Klas (Cypress).

Highlights: working in a QA team, cut regression testing on a link-in-bio platform from a full day to about 30 minutes with a suite of 100 automated Playwright tests; early local testing means a regression run now surfaces only 1–2 bugs, and two critical bugs were stopped before production; tests a local LLM (Llama 3) for product analytics with 100 hand-written prompts, reaching 97%+ answer accuracy after prompt-template fixes. Domains: SaaS creator platforms, e-commerce and product analytics. Languages: Serbian (native), English (C1). Open to remote.

Contact: markolosic1993@gmail.com

### Latest Articles

- [PetLink: The Pet Care App I Built and Tested End to End](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/petlink-pet-care-app/): Why I built PetLink, an Android app for dog and cat owners, how Gemini and Claude wrote and reviewed its React Native and Supabase code, and what testing my own product taught me.
- [Testing AI Features That See: QA for Image and Document Inputs](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/vision-ai-testing-image-inputs/): Vision AI features fail in two ways text-only QA misses: bad input images and confident hallucinations. Here's how to test for both.
- [Session-Based Exploratory Testing: How to Make Ad Hoc Testing Repeatable and Reportable](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/session-based-exploratory-testing/): How session-based test management turns unscripted exploratory testing into something you can plan, measure, and report on, with a worked charter example.
- [Load Testing for QA Teams: What k6 Catches, and What a Passing Threshold Can Still Hide](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/load-testing-qa-teams-k6-thresholds/): A practical k6 walkthrough for QA teams: scripting a load test, setting thresholds, and the pitfalls that make a green dashboard misleading.
- [Testing RAG Pipelines: Why Your Retrieval Step Needs Its Own Test Suite](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/testing-rag-pipelines-retrieval-evaluation/): RAG systems fail quietly when retrieval goes wrong. Here's how to test retrieval and generation separately, with a worked example and a metric to watch.
- [Testing File Uploads: The Edge Cases a Happy-Path Suite Walks Right Past](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/file-upload-testing-edge-cases/): Why file upload features break in production and how to test size limits, type spoofing, concurrency, and interrupted transfers.
- [Claude Fable 5.2 for Testing: Where the Advantages Are Real and Where They Stop](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/claude-fable-5-2-for-testing/): What Claude Fable 5.2 changes for QA work: long agentic runs, computer use, vision and cost, with the limits spelled out.
- [Test Pyramid or Testing Trophy: Picking the Shape That Matches Your Risk, Not the Diagram](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/test-pyramid-vs-testing-trophy/): The test pyramid and testing trophy give opposite advice on where to put your tests. Here's how to decide which shape actually fits your codebase.
- [Chaos Engineering for QA Teams: What a Game Day Actually Looks Like](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/chaos-engineering-game-day-qa-teams/): A practical look at chaos engineering tools and how to run a resilience game day without turning it into an outage.
- [Pairwise Testing: Cutting Thousands of Config Combinations Down to a Suite You Can Actually Run](https://markolosic.github.io/blog/pairwise-combinatorial-testing/): How pairwise and combinatorial testing shrink a combinatorial explosion into a small, high-coverage test suite, with a worked example and tool picks.
